<!-- pr-reviewer: 7741c194448a5fce0ccb7b5d05a19dfec4fc927c -->
Verdict: no blocker found. One run is open: the light lane was not run here (permission refused). Review label not set; the maintainer or the coordinator decides after the light run.

## What looks good
- Test-only change. Library code is not changed. The only non-test edit is the `#[path = "adaptive_troch_heavy_tests.rs"] mod heavy;` line at the end of `adaptive_troch_tests.rs`.
- I compared the six moved full tests with their old bodies by script (the old text with `super::super::` changed to `super::super::super::`). All six are byte-identical. No value, tolerance or loop count changed.
- Each full test has an ignore reason that names the lane (`heavy lane: motion heavy: lib (... s in debug, #3514)`). None is a known-fail test.
- Each twin is named `<full test>_light`, starts its reason with `light lane:`, and sits in the same file as its full test.
- `#[test]` count: 10 + 12 = 22 (16 before). No test is deleted. Files: 219 and 321 lines.
- Body: per-test table, `Changelog: none`, `Refs #3514` (no closing keyword).

## Results (merged with main 09ad779ee; trial merge was "Already up to date"), local, `-j 6`
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --lib adaptive_troch -- --test-threads=6` (debug) | 13 passed (10 module tests + 3 `adaptive_troch_level`), 0 failed, 12 ignored; 10.11 s test time |
| `cargo xtask gate light --dry-run` | `motion light: lib` lists the six new twins |
| `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run` | `motion heavy: lib` is listed |
| `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --lib --profile test -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask gate light --only "motion light: lib"` (release) | not run (permission refused) |

## Heavy lanes
- The six full tests: not run here. The PR body says the author ran each one once in release, 6 passed. I did not repeat it. The full heavy lane runs at the cut.
- Light twins: not run here. Not a pass. The PR body says 7 passed in 12 s on the author's machine.

## What each twin drops, and where that part still runs
1. `the_pocket_face_..._light`: one level (bottom -3) in place of two. The second level and the step-down between levels run only in release (full test).
2. `the_opened_bore_..._light`: the production lane only. The plain-bore post (> 4 mm2) and the stand-alone slot run only in the full test (release). A part of #1589 is covered in debug by `tests/trochoid_slot.rs` (`trochoid_wide_channel_leaves_no_post_at_the_start`) on a different band.
3. `without_lift_room_..._light`: the cut without lift room only. The default-helix cross-check (no "Entry setting" note) runs only in the full test.
4. `explicit_trochoidal_parameters_..._light`: 16x12 face in place of 30x16, and no explicit-`Retract` cut. The explicit-`Retract` rapid count (> 40) runs only in the full test (release). Twin 3 checks the retract-returns law through `retract_z: None`, not through the explicit parameter.
5. `custom_parameters_reach_..._light`: the 30x24 parallel layout only. The closed-lane ring layout of this test runs only in release. Debug has `tests/adaptive_troch_island.rs` (`ring_round_island_is_cleared_with_closed_lane`), which is not ignored, but it does not check the custom parameters.
6. `custom_return_feed_..._light`: 24x20 pocket in place of 30x24. Same law and limits.

Price of the move: these dropped parts now run only in the release lanes (the full tests at the cut). The PR body names the reduced cases. It does not say that the dropped parts have no debug run. Please add one sentence.

## Requested before merge
None blocking. Two notes:
1. `docs/decisions/3514-motion-slow-tests.md`, "Why": it says the six tests took 76 s to 334 s in debug (#3427) and gives no warning. The PR body says these times come from a parallel run: `without_lift_room_...` takes 14.7 s alone, not 72.5 s. Add that line to the decision file. The ignore reason of that test (`73 s in debug`) shows the contended number.
2. Note for slices B and C: by the PR's own numbers, `without_lift_room_...` is under 60 s alone in debug (14.7 s), and the module default run was already short (10 s). The 60 s rule did not need that move. The other five have no stand-alone debug time in the PR, so the 60 s rule is not proven for them either way. Slices B and C should measure each test alone before a move.

## Questions
- The `eprintln!` of the first full test stays in the full test only. This is fine.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
